p: The best escape room teams aren't the cleverest, they're the most organised. When the clock starts, don't all pile in on the first thing you see. Spread out, search every corner, and bring what you find back to one place. Then start making connections. If you're stuck on a lock, ask yourselves what you haven't used yet. Usually, the answer is staring right at you.

Escape rooms are a great fit for Liverpool's legendary sense of humour, too. You'll laugh at yourselves, you'll argue about who missed the obvious clue, and you'll probably want a rematch. Hen and stag groups love it as an afternoon activity before a big night out, and families find it a refreshing change from museum-hopping. Parking around the dock can fill up on busy days, so the train into Liverpool Central or James Street and a short walk down to the river is often the easier option.

Beyond the Albert Dock, the waterfront keeps on giving. The Museum of Liverpool at the Pier Head tells the story of the city, from its maritime past to its music and football, and it's free to visit. Mersey Ferries sail from the Pier Head across the river, with that famous view of the skyline on the way back. Head into town and you'll find the Cavern Quarter around Mathew Street, the heart of Beatles history, and the grand neoclassical St George's Hall opposite Lime Street station. Liverpool also boasts two remarkable cathedrals at either end of Hope Street, one a huge Gothic Anglican landmark, the other the striking modern Catholic Metropolitan Cathedral, both worth a look if you've got the time.
